detailed_rationale:
The Anup Engineering (demerged from Arvind Limited in 2018) makes heat exchangers, reactors, pressure vessels, columns & towers and industrial centrifuges for oil & gas, petrochemicals, LNG, fertilizers, chemicals, pharma, power, water, paper & pulp and aerospace clients - a genuine process-equipment capital-goods franchise tied to India's energy/chemicals capex cycle. The quant panel's own growth_divergence_flag (True) correctly flags that FY26 revenue growth of ~12% (to Rs 822 crore) is a sharp step-down from the 26% 3-year CAGR, and this research confirms it is real demand normalization after an unusually strong 2023-2025 capex up-cycle, not a data artifact - margin has compressed alongside it, with operating margin falling to ~18% in the most recent quarters from a historical 21-23%.

The more notable findings are on cash generation and leverage: free cash flow has been negative for multiple periods running (-Rs 51 crore as of March 2026, a trend since March 2025, not a single bad quarter), debtor days have stretched from 141 to 185 - large industrial/EPC clients paying more slowly - and borrowings jumped sharply from Rs 32 crore to Rs 110 crore (March 2025 to March 2026, +244%), even though the absolute leverage level remains low relative to the company's size (D/E ~0.16x, interest coverage ~19x per the quant panel). Together this reads as a capital-goods business coming off a supercycle peak, now facing normalized order intake, compressed margins, and working-capital strain as it executes its existing order book - a real and fairly common pattern for this sector after a strong multi-year run, not evidence of a broken franchise. Promoter holding has drifted down modestly (42.91% to 40.92% since September 2023) - a gentle trend, not an alarming one. Order-book figures were not available in public sources for direct confirmation.
recommendation_rationale: Quant scores this Hold on both windows (53.2 / 49.5), and the growth_divergence_flag is already doing its job here - the quant model itself correctly discounts the eye-catching 3-year CAGR via a much weaker 1-year growth score. My research confirms this is genuine post-cycle-peak normalization (margin compression, negative FCF, stretched receivables) rather than a hidden data problem the model is missing, so I see no basis to escalate; a properly cautious Hold that does not extrapolate the historical 26% growth rate forward.
summary: Anup Engineering makes pressure vessels and heat exchangers for the oil & gas, petrochemical, fertilizer and chemicals capex cycle, and just came off an unusually strong multi-year run - growth has now normalized to a more modest pace, margins have compressed a bit, and the company is currently generating negative free cash flow while receivables from large industrial clients take longer to collect. None of this looks alarming on its own for a capital-goods business working through its order book after a supercycle, but it does mean the historical 26% growth rate is not the right guide to what comes next. We rate this a Hold.
positive_para: A genuine, diversified process-equipment franchise (heat exchangers, pressure vessels, reactors) serving structurally growing end-markets (energy, LNG, specialty chemicals, fertilizers) with real multi-year capex tailwinds behind India's energy-security and chemicals investment cycle; leverage remains low in absolute terms (D/E ~0.16x, interest coverage ~19x) even after the recent debt increase, giving room to fund working capital through the current stretch; promoter holding has only drifted modestly, not fallen sharply.
negative_para: Free cash flow has been negative for more than one period running, not just a single quarter, and debtor days have stretched meaningfully (141 to 185) - both signs of real, currently-ongoing working-capital strain rather than a one-off. Operating margin has compressed from the low-20s% to ~18%, and revenue growth has stepped down sharply from the 26% 3-year CAGR to ~12% in the latest year - the strong 2023-2025 cycle appears to be normalizing, and there is no order-book data available in this pass to confirm how much revenue visibility remains at the prior growth rate. Borrowings more than tripled year-on-year (off a low base), a trend worth monitoring even though absolute leverage remains modest today.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~39x trailing earnings, the multiple still assumes a return to something closer to the historical high-growth trajectory rather than the ~12% pace just delivered - a reasonable bet given the structural energy/chemicals capex tailwind, but not yet confirmed by the current working-capital and margin trends, which are moving the wrong way for now. Fair-to-rich: defensible if the cycle re-accelerates and cash conversion normalizes, stretched if the current negative-FCF/margin-compression pattern persists.

technical_commentary: A dramatic 2023-2024 parabolic spike (Rs 374 to a Rs 3,717 ATH, ~10x) occurred on surprisingly light and declining volume -- itself a quality flag on that advance -- and the eighteen months since the November 2024 top have been genuinely choppy and directionless, swinging as much as ~48% either way month to month (e.g. Rs 1,571 to Rs 2,331) without resolving into a new trend. The tangled MA stack (price below the 20-month average but above the 10- and 40-month) is consistent with a structure still searching for direction post-blow-off.
